note: PAREN `t', AND THE COST IT CARRIES. Emacs answers (0 "ab" "ab"): the alternation is wrapped in a CAPTURING group, so the whole match is also group 1 -- which shifts every group number in a caller's surrounding regexp by one. This is a CONTRACT case: it compiles what `regexp-opt' returned with the running engine and asks what it matched, because Emacs' own text ("\\(ab?\\)", measured) is its optimizer's output and matching that spelling would encode the optimizer here -- the rule `frontier-regexp-opt' set and this group keeps. U.1a implemented the argument and kg answers this: its `\(ab\|a\)' is a different spelling of the same contract.
